exposure: delivery mode (spontaneous vaginal, operative vaginal, elective caesarean, secondary caesarean, emergency caesarean)
outcome: neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions due to RDS
cohort: The study included 37,110 live-born infants between 34+0 and 41+6 weeks gestational age from the University Hospitals of Zurich and Basel.
finding: The incidence of respiratory distress syndrome was significantly higher after an elective caesarean delivery, particularly in infants born before 39 weeks gestational age, compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean delivery was associated with an up to threefold higher risk of respiratory distress syndrome in infants born before 39 weeks gestational age compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
